_comment: Mutations that put the AGPL-3.0 source offer's two OVERSTATEMENTS back
into frontend/source.html.
The defect (measured, reviewed on the Copilot engine): the archive
link is https://github.com/DiverseInc/DepthSight/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz
-- a SNAPSHOT OF THE TIP of the branch, not a history. The running
service is deployed from `main`, and the deploy lands a few minutes
AFTER a merge, so between a merge and its deploy the archive is the
NEWER tree and the running build's tree is genuinely not in it. The
page used to claim otherwise.
M1 restores the old archive-identity claim in the 'Where to get the
source code' note: 'the archive link above are the source code of
the running service'. Killed by
test_the_page_does_not_say_the_archive_is_the_running_service.
M2 restores the old unconditional published-match claim in the
'Which source code matches the version you are running' section:
'and it is the published match for the code you are talking to'.
Killed by
test_the_page_does_not_call_main_the_published_match_unconditionally.
Both needles are SINGLE-LINE strings and each occurs EXACTLY ONCE in
frontend/source.html (asserted before use); a needle that matched two
sites would make the mutation meaningless.
Run with:  python tools/mutation_harness.py tools/mutations/source_offer_snapshot_claim.json
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.

mutations.label: M1: the source offer claims the archive link IS the source code of the running service (the old overstatement)
mutations.needle: the archive link above is a snapshot of the tip of
mutations.replace: the archive link above are the source code of the running service, and so is the tip of

mutations.label: M2: the source offer calls main the published match for the code you are talking to, unconditionally (the old overstatement)
mutations.needle: and it is the exact published match
mutations.replace: and it is the published match for the code you are talking to
